service_boundary: Represents managed generative inference on Vertex AI, not Gemini Apps, Google AI Studio, individual Gemini releases, or the broader Vertex AI agent platform.
regional_controls: Availability, data residency, and processing location depend on the selected model, endpoint type, and Google Cloud region; serverless and self-deployed Model Garden paths have different boundaries.
retention_controls: Data governance follows the selected Vertex AI service, project configuration, model publisher, and Google Cloud terms; customers must review model- and feature-specific documentation rather than infer one platform-wide rule.
routing: The platform provides a common cloud control plane across model sources, but the reviewed service is not represented as an automatic latency- or price-based cross-provider router.
customization: Model Garden supports managed APIs, tuning, and deployment paths for eligible Google, partner, open, and customer models, including dedicated endpoints for self-deployed models.
strengths: Model Garden combines first-party, partner, open, and customer deployment paths with Google Cloud governance.
Serverless, provisioned, batch, and dedicated deployment choices cover distinct production needs.
tradeoffs: Serving mode, region support, terms, and operational responsibility differ substantially across model categories.
The broad platform boundary requires model-specific review before treating any capability as universal.

evidence.label: Generative AI on Vertex AI overview

response_integrity.note: Scoped to generated media, not text or tool-call responses. The Content Credentials guide states: "This technology utilizes cryptographically signed metadata to provide secure and verifiable records of a media file's origin and any changes it's undergone. Being cryptographically signed, this information is tamper-evident." Ordinary chat and tool-call responses carry no signature.
response_integrity.scope: Vertex AI generative-AI content-credentials guide, for Vertex AI Generative AI

upstream_disclosure.note: The partner-models usage guide describes how to call third-party models but does not state whether the model's publisher (Anthropic, Meta, and others hosted through Vertex) receives the request content or whether it stays within Google's own infrastructure.
upstream_disclosure.scope: Vertex AI partner-models usage guide, for Vertex AI Generative AI

credential_handling.note: The service offers no customer-supplied upstream-key path: "To use Gemini on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, authenticate by using a Google Cloud API key or application default credentials."
credential_handling.scope: Vertex AI generative-AI API-keys guide, for Vertex AI Generative AI

cache_isolation.note: The data-governance page states: "By default, Google's published Gemini models cache Customer Data (inputs, outputs, and derived data) in-memory to reduce latency and accelerate responses. This data is stored only in-memory (not at-rest), is isolated at the project level, and has a 24-hour TTL."
cache_isolation.scope: Vertex AI generative-AI data-governance page, for Vertex AI Generative AI

vulnerability_disclosure.note: Google's Cloud Vulnerability Reward Program states its scope: "In principle, any Google Cloud product or web service that handles reasonably sensitive user data is intended to be in scope." It does not name the service individually.
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: Google Cloud Vulnerability Reward Program rules, for Vertex AI Generative AI

independent_audit.note: The Google Cloud SOC 2 scope page names the service, under its current product name: "Generative AI on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Generative AI on Vertex AI)".
independent_audit.scope: Google Cloud SOC 2 compliance page, for Vertex AI Generative AI

resolved.summary: The current data-governance page documents project-level, in-memory, 24-hour caching; the paper detected no caching for the tested Google models at the time of its 2024 audit, so this is not a finding of unsafe sharing.
